board.name: Rhode Island Board of Licensure for Physician Assistants (RI Department of Health)

licence.title: Physician Assistant (PA)
licence.renewalDeadline: Licence expires June 30 of every odd-numbered year; renewal application due on or before June 1 of the odd-numbered year

ce.hoursNote: 25 hours of approved CME annually (R.I. Gen. Laws 5-54-22; board page restates it), so 50 across the two year licence. The statute sets the annual accumulation period as October 1 to September 30, while regulation 24.8(B) sets July 1 to June 30 and 24.8(A) omits the period word ('every years'). Which annual window RIDOH audits against is not yet verified; the hour total (25 per year) is confirmed.
ce.categoryRules: Approved CME means a program approved by AAPA, ACCME/AMA, AAFP, AOA, or another board approved program (5-54-2(3)). No Category 1 minimum split is stated.
ce.nccpaNote: NCCPA exam is required for initial licensure; maintenance of NCCPA certification is listed only as something the board may require for reactivation after 2+ years out of practice (24.6(E)). Not a renewal requirement in the regulation.

topicMandates.topic: Best practices in opioid prescribing (appropriate prescribing for pain, pharmacology, adverse events, dependence, tolerance, SUD, alternatives)
topicMandates.appliesTo: Any practitioner who prescribes a Schedule II opioid; due before renewal of the controlled substance registration or two years, whichever is longer. Category 1 CME or equivalent. The rule exempts practitioners who completed DATA 2000 waiver training and hold an active DEA 'X' designation (the X waiver no longer exists federally, so the exemption covers only those who already qualified).

topicMandates.topic: ER/LA opioid analgesic REMS compliant education
topicMandates.appliesTo: Practitioners prescribing long-acting or extended-release opioids

ce.controlledSubstanceCe: 8 hours one-time Category 1 (or equivalent) opioid prescribing training for any practitioner prescribing Schedule II opioids (216-RICR-20-20-4.4(P)); plus federal DEA one-time 8 hour SUD training (MATE).

practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: No written agreement filed with the board. PAs practice in collaboration with physicians; the degree of collaboration is determined by the practice (physician employer, group, hospital credentialing). A physician must be accessible at all times for consultation.
practice.notes: RI enacted the PA Licensure Compact; the board page says it is not currently operational.

prescribing.separateAuthorityRegistration: RI Controlled Substances Registration (Board of Pharmacy, RIDOH) plus DEA registration; PDMP registration is a condition of initial and renewed CS registration. Interval: statute 21-28-3.02(a) says 'obtain annually', regulation 4.5(A) says at intervals not to exceed two years; the actual RIDOH renewal cycle is not yet verified.
prescribing.ceForPrescribers: 8 hours one-time opioid prescribing CME for Schedule II opioid prescribers; ER/LA opioid REMS education for long-acting opioid prescribers

board.name: Rhode Island Board of Nurse Registration and Nursing Education (RI Department of Health)

rn.renewalDeadline: Expires March 1 of every other year following original licensure; renewal application before February 15
rn.nlcNote: Rejoined the NLC January 1, 2024 (board page). The statute (ch. 5-34.3) still marks its compact sections 'Expires January 1, 2027'. As of 2026-10-01 no extension was found; if none is enacted, RI multistate licensure ends January 1, 2027. Not yet verified either way.

topicMandates.appliesTo: All nurses renewing (2 of the 10 hours); stated on the board page, not found in the regulation text

topicMandates.topic: Alzheimer's disease and cognitive impairment (diagnosis, treatment, care)
topicMandates.appliesTo: All nurses licensed under chapter 5-34 (includes APRNs); statutory deadline October 1, 2023

aprn.title: APRN-CNP (Advanced Practice Registered Nurse, Certified Nurse Practitioner)
aprn.separateLicenceOrCertificate: Separate APRN licence issued by the Board of Nursing; requires a current RN licence or multistate privilege
aprn.ceNote: The regulation sets 10 hours per two years for every licence renewed under the Act; no separate APRN hour total is stated.
aprn.pharmacologyNote: No pharmacology hour requirement appears in the current regulation (216-RICR-40-05-3) or statute. Vendor pages citing 30 pharmacology hours every 6 years could not be confirmed in a primary source.
aprn.nationalCertificationNote: Current national certification verified at renewal; exception for nurse practitioners without prescriptive privileges licensed as of June 17, 2013.

topicMandates.appliesTo: APRNs who prescribe Schedule II opioids (216-RICR-20-20-4.4(P)); DATA 2000 waiver training qualifies and active X designation holders are exempt (4.4(P)(2))

unverified: PA CME accumulation window: statute 5-54-22 says October 1 to September 30, regulation 24.8(B) says July 1 to June 30. The 25 hours per year total is confirmed; which window RIDOH audits is not.
Controlled substance registration interval: statute 21-28-3.02(a) says annually, regulation 216-RICR-20-20-4.5(A) says not to exceed two years; actual RIDOH cycle not confirmed.
Nurse Licensure Compact: statute still shows the January 1, 2027 sunset on 2026-10-01; no extension found, and none confirmed absent.
RN 2 hours substance abuse per cycle: stated on the RIDOH Nurses page (primary), but not in 216-RICR-40-05-3 or 5-34-19; statutory basis not located.
APRN pharmacology CE: none in current regulation or statute; vendor claims of 30 hours per 6 years remain unconfirmed and should not be shown.
PA: whether current NCCPA certification is accepted in lieu of the 25 hours is not stated anywhere loaded; treat as not accepted until confirmed.
Whether the single 10 hour requirement satisfies both the RN and APRN licence renewals or applies to each licence separately is not stated.
verificationCorrections: PA CME: added the statutory accumulation window (5-54-22: October 1 to September 30), which conflicts with regulation 24.8(B) (July 1 to June 30); 25 hours per year confirmed, audit window marked not yet verified.
PA licence: added 5-54-11(b) statute fact; the odd-numbered year comes only from regulation 24.6.
CS registration interval: statute 21-28-3.02(a) says annually, regulation 4.5(A) says not to exceed two years; researcher reported only the regulation. Both recorded, cycle marked not yet verified.
Added PDMP registration as a condition of CS registration (4.5(A)(6), 21-28-3.02(c)) for PA and APRN.
Opioid 8 hour one-time rule: added the DATA 2000 / X designation exemption (4.4(P)(2)).
ER/LA opioid REMS education: researcher listed it without a fact; added primary cite 216-RICR-20-20-4.4(N)(1) and added it to the APRN mandates too.
Alzheimer one-time hour: confirmed it does not apply to PAs (statute names physicians and nurses only); added board page fact (one hour per career, effective August 1, 2019) for nurses.
NLC: re-loaded statute on 2026-10-01; sunset January 1, 2027 still in text, no extension found; note strengthened (multistate licensure would end in 3 months absent an extension).
Added PA Licensure Compact not operational (board page), RN CE provider and 4 year record rules (3.5), and APRN 5 business day certification lapse notice (3.9).
RIDOH board pages blocked curl (403); re-loaded them in a browser and confirmed the 25 hour, 10 hour, 2 hour substance abuse and NLC statements.
